issues.issue_title: ADC overrun (OVR) interrupt never enabled in ADC interrupt mode
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: ADC overrun (OVR) interrupt never enabled in ADC interrupt mode
Context: repo=stm32f3xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=ADC, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=4
Root cause: ST Internal Reference: 215351 Hello @Nor-Fla, As mentioned in the comment above /* If overrun is set to overwrite previous data (default setting), */ /* overrun interrupt is not activated (overrun event is not considered */ /* as an error).
Fix: Hello, in the function HAL_ADC_Start_IT(.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, ADC, bug_report, high, bug, internal bug tracker, HAL_ADC_Start_IT, ADC_IT_OVR

Technical details:
Hello, in the function HAL_ADC_Start_IT(...) the overrun interrupt never gets enabled. To solve the issue, I think this line: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f3xx-hal-driver/blob/9a2ddd0988e817511a27f88fdaeebc04ff2587e1/Src/stm32f3xx_hal_adc_ex.c#L2144 must be changed to __HAL_ADC_ENABLE_IT(hadc, ADC_IT_OVR);. Regards, Norbert

Key comments:
ST Internal Reference: 215351 Hello @Nor-Fla, As mentioned in the comment above /* If overrun is set to overwrite previous data (default setting), */ /* overrun interrupt is not activated (overrun event is not considered */ /* as an error). */ /* (cf ref manual "Managing conversions without using the DMA and */ /* without overrun ") */ if (hadc->Init.Overrun == ADC_OVR_DATA_PRESERVED) { __HAL_ADC_DISABLE_IT(hadc, ADC_IT_OVR); } The instruction, please refer to the reference manual, section "Managing conversions without using the DMA and without overrun" When OVRMOD = 1 (hadc->Init.Overrun == ADC_OVR_DATA_PRESERVED), the software should ignore the OVR flag. To ensure this, the corresponding interrupt is disabled using the following function: __HAL_ADC_DISABLE_IT(hadc, ADC_IT_OVR); ==> As a result, the implementation of HAL_ADC_Start_IT() depends on how the user configures the Overrun parameter in the Init structure. This behavior is correctly managed in the current code. Hello @RJMSTM , it's just the other way

issues.issue_title: I2C buffer overflow or IRQ flooding, when receiving extra bytes as slave in interrupt mode
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: I2C buffer overflow or IRQ flooding, when receiving extra bytes as slave in interrupt mode
Context: repo=stm32f3xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=3
Root cause: Hello again @Nor-Fla, Regarding this issue, could you please share more details about your project?
Fix: Hello, I want to receive some data via I2C as slave in interrupt mode.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, bug_report, medium, bug, invalid, i2c, HAL_I2C_Slave_Receive_IT, RXDR, RXNE

Technical details:
Hello, I want to receive some data via I2C as slave in interrupt mode. So I call HAL_I2C_Slave_Receive_IT(...). It works fine, as long as I receive the expected amount of bytes or less. But if I receive **more** than the expected number of bytes, I get a receive buffer overflow here: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f3xx-hal-driver/blob/9a2ddd0988e817511a27f88fdaeebc04ff2587e1/Src/stm32f3xx_hal_i2c.c#L6395 I think, this issue could be fixed by moving the read out of RXDR into the receive buffer inside the condition here: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f3xx-hal-driver/blob/9a2ddd0988e817511a27f88fdaeebc04ff2587e1/Src/stm32f3xx_hal_i2c.c#L6400 and adding an else branch where RXDR is read into a dummy variable to clear the RXNE flag. Regards, Norbert

Key comments:
Hello again @Nor-Fla, Regarding this issue, could you please share more details about your project? In the meantime, I will share your proposal with our team for further analysis. Hello @KRASTM , we have a system of 2 custom boards connected via I2C. One is based on a STM32F303ZE and the other on a STM32G0B1RE. The F3 board works as I2C master and I call the polling HAL API function HAL_I2C_Master_Transmit(...) for data transmission. The G0 board is the I2C slave, where I call HAL_I2C_Slave_Receive_IT(...) to receive data. As the G0 board wasn't built, yet, I used a F3 Nucleo for prototyping. I wanted to see, what happens, if the master sends more bytes, than the slave expects. So I debugged the HAL and measured the I2C signals with an oscilloscope. In the case of 1 additional byte, I could see, that the slave ACKs the extra byte and the master sends the STOP condition. In the call of I2C_Slave_ISR_IT(...) for the extra byte, only the RXNE flag is set. But because hi2c->XferCount is 0, RXDR is NOT read and so RXNE is NOT cleared! Then the slave recognizes the STOP condition. In the following call to I2C_Slave_ISR_IT(...) both RXNE and STOPF flags are set. The STOPF flag is han

issues.issue_title: Polling I2C EEPROM for internal write cycle immediately returns HAL_ERROR
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Polling I2C EEPROM for internal write cycle immediately returns HAL_ERROR
Context: repo=stm32f3xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=2
Root cause: Hello @Nor-Fla, Thank you for the report.
Fix: Hello, after writing to an I2C EEPROM using HAL_I2C_Mem_Write(.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, spotted before customer, i2c, EEPROM, HAL_I2C_Mem_Write, HAL_I2C_IsDeviceReady, HAL_ERROR, NACK

Technical details:
Hello, after writing to an I2C EEPROM using HAL_I2C_Mem_Write(...), I want to poll for the end of its internal write cycle and call HAL_I2C_IsDeviceReady(...). But inside this function the call to I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout(...) here: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f3xx-hal-driver/blob/9a2ddd0988e817511a27f88fdaeebc04ff2587e1/Src/stm32f3xx_hal_i2c.c#L3344 fails, because the call to I2C_IsErrorOccurred(...), which was added to I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout(...) in v1.5.8, returns HAL_ERROR, because of the NACK flag set at that moment. But here the NACK flag is NOT an error, but a feature of the I2C EERPOM, telling me, that the internal write cycle is still going on. I think, this issue could be fixed by moving the clearing of the NACK flag from here: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f3xx-hal-driver/blob/9a2ddd0988e817511a27f88fdaeebc04ff2587e1/Src/stm32f3xx_hal_i2c.c#L3350 right before the call to I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout(...). Regards, Norbert

Key comments:
Hello @Nor-Fla, Thank you for the report. It has indeed been fixed internally and will be published shortly. ST Internal Reference: 181377 Hello @KRASTM, thanks for your reply. Meanwhile, I found the same issue in the STM32CubeG0 HAL (https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32g0xx-hal-driver/tree/master). Do you know that internally, too, or should I open an issue there? Norbert Hello @Nor-Fla, Indeed, the same applies to the G0 series and others, following an old ticket. Though you are welcome to open an issue in the G0 HAL repository for the trace. Fixed in commit: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f3xx-hal-driver/commit/74e7b5f359e869445a8f523f505f863117cbed5e

issues.issue_title: LL: OPAMP functional modes assert incomplete
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: LL: OPAMP functional modes assert incomplete
Context: repo=stm32f3xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=medium, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=1
Root cause: Hi @diggit, Thank you for this report.
Fix: **Describe the set-up** * custom board, not directly relevant to issue * GCC 10.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, usage_question, medium, question, GCC, LL_OPAMP_MODE_STANDALONE, OPAMP, LL_OPAMP_MODE_FOLLOWER, OPAMP_CSR_VMSEL_1, OPAMP_CSR_VMSEL_0, LL_OPAMP_MODE_PGA, PGA

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** * custom board, not directly relevant to issue * GCC 10.2, cmake, ninja **Describe the bug** [These two functional modes](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f3xx_hal_driver/blob/master/Inc/stm32f3xx_ll_opamp.h#L141) are not allowed by [checking macro](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f3xx_hal_driver/blob/master/Src/stm32f3xx_ll_opamp.c#L52) and causes [assertion](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f3xx_hal_driver/blob/master/Src/stm32f3xx_ll_opamp.c#L148) when used. Funtional modes: c #define LL_OPAMP_MODE_STANDALONE (0x00000000U) /*!< OPAMP functional mode, OPAMP operation in standalone */ #define LL_OPAMP_MODE_FOLLOWER (OPAMP_CSR_VMSEL_1 | OPAMP_CSR_VMSEL_0) /*!< OPAMP functional mode, OPAMP operation in follower */ #define LL_OPAMP_MODE_PGA (OPAMP_CSR_VMSEL_1) /*!< OPAMP functional mode, OPAMP operation in PGA */ #define LL_OPAMP_MODE_PGA_EXT_FILT_IO0 (OPAMP_CSR_PGGAIN_3 | OPAMP_CSR_VMSEL_1) /*!< OPAMP functional mode, OPAMP operation in PGA with external filtering on OPAMP input IO0. */ #define LL_OPAMP_MODE_PGA_EXT_FILT_IO1 (OPAMP_CSR_PGGAIN_3 | OPAMP_CSR_PGGAIN_2 | OPAMP_CSR_VMSEL_1) /*!< OPAMP functional mode, OPAMP operation in PGA with external filtering on OPAMP input IO1. */ Macro used in assert. c #define IS_LL_OPAMP_FUNCTIONAL_MODE(__FUNCTIONAL_MODE__) \ ( ((__FUNCTIONAL_MODE__) == LL_OPAMP_MODE_STANDALONE) \ || ((__FUNCTIONAL_MODE__) == LL_OPAMP_MODE_FOLLOWER) \ || ((__FUNCTIONAL_MODE__) == LL_OPAMP_MODE_PGA) \ ) Clearly, macro does not accept LL_OPAMP_MODE_PGA_EXT_FILT_IO0 and LL_OPAMP_MODE_PGA_EXT_FILT_IO1 functional modes. **How To Reproduce** 1. have code like c LL_OPAMP_InitTypeDef OPAMP_InitStruct {}; OPAMP_InitStruct.FunctionalMode = LL_OPAMP_MODE_PGA_EXT_FILT_IO1; OPAMP_InitStruct.InputNonInverting = LL_OPAMP_INPUT_NONINVERT_IO0; OPAMP_InitStruct.InputInverting = LL_OPAMP_INPUT_INVERT_IO1; LL_OPAMP_Init(OPAMP2, &OPAMP_InitStruct); 2. enable assertions by defining USE_FULL_ASSERT 3. compile and run 4. assertion occurs on valid functional mode

Key comments:
Hi @diggit, Thank you for this report. The issue has been forwarded to our development teams. We will get back to you as soon as they provide us with their feedback. Hi @diggit, Referring to our development team, to be able to use the PGA external filtering, OPAMP should be configured in 2 steps: 1. Use LL_OPAMP_Init() with the FunctionalMode param configured as **"LL_OPAMP_MODE_PGA"**. 2. Use the LL_OPAMP_SetFunctionalMode() to configure the PGA external filtering with the desired config **LL_OPAMP_MODE_PGA_EXT_FILT_IO**0 or **LL_OPAMP_MODE_PGA_EXT_FILT_IO1**. Thus, the actual implementation of the IS_LL_OPAMP_FUNCTIONAL_MODE is correct, the macro should not accept LL_OPAMP_MODE_PGA_EXT_FILT_IO0 and LL_OPAMP_MODE_PGA_EXT_FILT_IO1 . However, we agree to say that the driver is not clear enough regarding this. Our development teams will work on it and will propose some enhancement. Thank you once again for your contribution and thank you for drawing our attention to this.
